claims.explanation: U-18666A is a lysosomotropic amphiphile that blocks cholesterol egress from late endosomes/lysosomes, phenocopying NPC1 loss-of-function and causing lysosomal cholesterol accumulation, impaired LDL-receptor downregulation, and altered sterol/neurotransmitter metabolism. Cancer lines that depend on lysosomal cholesterol trafficking and NPC1-pathway function (e.g., high NPC1/sterol-sensing-domain activity, active SREBP/LDLR uptake, or lysosomal lipid storage capacity) are expected to be most sensitive, while lines with low lysosomal cholesterol flux or compensatory sterol synthesis are protected.

features.basis: U-18666A phenocopies NPC1 loss-of-function by blocking lysosomal cholesterol egress; high NPC1-pathway dependence predicts sensitivity
NPC2 binds lysosomal cholesterol and works with NPC1; its activity is required for the same trafficking step U-18666A inhibits
U-18666A blocks LDL-stimulated cholesterol esterification and LDL-receptor downregulation, so lines with high LDL uptake flux are more affected
U-18666A was annotated as an oxidosqualene cyclase inhibitor; high SQLE expression may buffer against sterol synthesis blockade
Desmosterol-to-cholesterol conversion is the step blocked by U-18666A; high DHCR24 activity could compensate for sterol synthesis inhibition
SREBP-2-driven sterol synthesis can compensate for lysosomal cholesterol deprivation and oxidosqualene cyclase inhibition
Cholesterol efflux capacity may reduce lysosomal free cholesterol accumulation caused by U-18666A
ACAT/sterol O-acyltransferase esterifies free cholesterol and may limit toxic unesterified lysosomal cholesterol accumulation
Lysosomal protease activity and lysosomal capacity are central to the U-18666A-induced lipid-filled lysosome phenotype
Damaging NPC1 mutations already impair lysosomal cholesterol egress, reducing the incremental effect of U-18666A
Loss of NPC2 cholesterol binding mimics the drug's block, so mutant lines should be less responsive
Damaging LDLR mutations reduce LDL-cholesterol delivery to lysosomes, the substrate pool U-18666A acts on
